page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor with x86_64 architecture, it allocates 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core on a dedicated basis. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 instruction and data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate a strong single-core CPU profile, with stress-ng single-core performance ranking in the top 25 percent. However, multi-core scaling is relatively weak, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the bottom 25 percent. Memory bandwidth is also a bottleneck, with uncached read and write speeds registering at 34.82 GB/sec and 15.16 GB/sec respectively, placing them in the bottom 25 percent. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels, as do Passmark CPU and memory scores.

Given its hardware profile, the c3d-standard-4 is suited for general-purpose workloads that rely on single-core performance rather than massive parallel processing or high memory throughput. Suitable applications include lightweight web serving, text processing, and small-scale LLM inference using models under 1B parameters. It is less optimal for database operations, software compilation, or medium-to-large language model inference due to weak multi-threaded scaling and low memory bandwidth. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated AMD EPYC cores offer reliable compute for entry-level workloads, though resource-intensive tasks may experience performance trade-offs.
